title: Local Defects and the Topology of the Haldane Model
abstract: We investigate the interplay between local defects and topology in the Haldane model within the framework of the tenfold classification. The Haldane model realizes a Chern-insulating phase characterized by an integer topological invariant ($C=\pm 1$) and supports chiral edge states. Introducing vacancies gives rise to localized states at the defect sites, classified by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant $ν= C\cdot m,\mathrm{mod},2$, where $m=N_A-N_B$ is the net sublattice imbalance of the vacancy configuration: an odd imbalance hosts a protected zero-energy mode, whereas an even imbalance does not. We identify three independent experimental signatures that distinguish these topological defect states from trivial (adatom) defects. First, vacancy-induced states exhibit characteristic dislocations in their wavefunction profiles that track the phase winding associated with the defect. Second, a fractional charge of $e/2$ accumulates at vacancy sites, while no such charge appears at adatoms. Third, the probability current circulating around a vacancy-induced state flows in the opposite direction to that of chiral edge states, in direct analogy with the current reversal produced by a vortex in a $p$-wave superconductor. All three signatures are in quantitative agreement with the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ prediction.
summary: This work analyzes how vacancies introduce localized topological structures into the Chern-insulating Haldane model. The key finding is that a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant, determined by sublattice imbalance, dictates whether zero-energy modes exist at the defect site. This prediction is robustly confirmed through three independent physical measurements: wavefunction geometry, fractional charge accumulation, and current flow reversal.
main_problem: The paper investigates how local defects (vacancies) modify the topological properties of the Haldane model, specifically examining the interplay between bulk topology and defect-induced topology.
main_result:
A $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant ($
u$) governs the presence of protected zero-energy modes at vacancies, which is confirmed by three independent experimental signatures: wavefunction dislocations, fractional charge accumulation, and opposite circulating probability currents.
method:
The analysis uses theoretical tools including the tenfold classification framework, Chern numbers ($C$), $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants ($
u$), and index theorems to derive relationships between bulk and defect topology.
model_or_system: The system is the Haldane model on a honeycomb lattice, which realizes a Chern-insulating phase. Defects studied include vacancies (bond removal) and adatoms (potential addition).
key_observables:
Chern number ($C=\pm 1$), $\mathbb{Z}_2$ defect invariant ($
u = C \cdot m \pmod 2$), zero-energy modes, fractional charge ($e/2$), and probability current direction.
important_parameters:
Sublattice imbalance $m = N_A - N_B$, which dictates the value of $
u$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on low-energy effective descriptions using Weyl symbols and assumes the applicability of topological invariants derived from the tenfold classification.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate the clean Haldane spectrum, the appearance of zero-energy modes for single vacancies ($
u=1$), mode splitting for two vacancies ($
u=0$), wavefunction dislocations tracking phase winding, and charge/current distributions confirming the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ prediction.
paper_structure:
The paper establishes the bulk topology ($C$) and then introduces defects. It derives the coupling formula ($
u = C \cdot m \pmod 2$) and presents three complementary diagnostics (dislocations, fractional charge, current reversal) that all confirm this topological classification.
why_interesting: The rigorous demonstration of multiple, distinct physical signatures confirming a single mathematical invariant ($\mathbb{Z}_2$) provides a powerful general principle for characterizing topological defects in condensed matter systems, applicable beyond the specific Haldane model.

FIG. 5. Haldane model with two vacancies on the same sub- lattice (NA = 2, NB = 0, ν = 0). Left: energy spectrum showing two defect-induced modes (green) that hybridize and split symmetrically about zero energy, with edge states (blue) and bulk modes (red) also visible. The two modes are lifted from zero energy because the Z2 invariant ν = 0 provides no topological protection. Right: spatial probability density of one of the hybridized modes, showing localization around the two vacancy sites.
